consensus_findings.description: Critical: The executable work-package DAG contradicts tasks.md: wp-prioritize and wp-integration can start without wp-producers, even though candidate ranking depends on all three producer implementations and integration explicitly exercises and mirrors them.
The plan correctly defines full-batch validation, atomic replacement, stable ordering, collision handling, and transaction-safe existing-roadmap intake as explicit executable contracts.

Critical: Explore-feature is specified to emit the "exact hinted or derived change ID" with no prefix normalization, but the skill instructs agents to create `fix-` opportunities, which the canonical schema pattern rejects, and D2's fail-closed batch validation then discards every candidate in the run. skills/explore-feature/SKILL.md:189 says cross-interface inconsistencies suggest `fix-` opportunities, while SKILL.md:269 declares the prefix set as add-/update-/refactor-/remove-. openspec/schemas/candidate-work.schema.json constrains suggested_change_id to `^(add|update|remove|refactor)-...`. Because design.md:26 requires the writer to validate the full list and preserve the prior file on failure, one `fix-` shortlist entry makes the whole sidecar unwritable, not just that entry. design.md:81 states a slug rule only for bug-scrub; improve-harness and explore-feature have no stated prefix derivation at all.

Critical: The new-roadmap intake path is specified only at item granularity, so the enclosing roadmap document has no defined `roadmap_id` or `source_proposal` and the scaffolded change has no defined capability. openspec/schemas/roadmap.schema.json:7 requires schema_version, roadmap_id, source_proposal, and items at the top level, but the D5 mapping table (design.md:56-64) covers seven item fields and stops. A candidate-work stub carries no proposal path; its only free-form fields are `tags` and `provenance.source_artifact`. Separately, skills/plan-roadmap/scripts/scaffolder.py:188 resolves the spec-delta capability directory from `item.capability` and falls back to `_slugify(roadmap_id)`; the candidate schema has no capability field and the mapping table does not populate one, so a candidate-derived change scaffolds its spec delta under a capability directory that does not exist in openspec/specs/. specs/roadmap-orchestration/spec.md:12 only asserts a schema-valid roadmap *item*, so no scenario catches this.

Critical: Explore-feature blockers are mapped into `depends_on`, but that field is prose in the source artifact and is interpreted as an exact change ID by both consumers, so explore-feature candidates become permanently blocked and un-intakeable. skills/explore-feature/SKILL.md:270 defines `blocked-by` as holding "existing change-ids, missing infra, unresolved design decisions", i.e. free text alongside identifiers. design.md:91 maps blockers into the stub. design.md:100-102 then resolves dependencies by exact change ID against the batch, roadmap items, and archives, marking unknown ones blocked, and design.md:126 makes an unresolvable dependency a hard refusal at intake. An opportunity blocked by "unresolved design decision on retry semantics" therefore ranks as blocked forever and can never be approved into the roadmap.

Critical: Task 4.2 runs skills/install.sh, which validates the install manifest before syncing, and the new shared dependency will fail that validation with no package holding write access to the manifest. skills/install.sh:219 invokes shared/validate_install_manifest.py before any mirror sync. That validator detects cross-skill references via the `<skill-base-dir>/../<name>` idiom (validate_install_manifest.py:30) and errors with "cross-skill dependency is not declared" for any undeclared pair (validate_install_manifest.py:277-280). skills/install-manifest.json currently has no `cross_skill_dependencies` entry for bug-scrub, improve-harness, or prioritize-proposals, and D2 makes all of them consume skills/shared/candidate_work.py. No package in this plan lists skills/install-manifest.json in write_allow: wp-contracts (lines 39-43) allows only shared/candidate_work.py and the prioritize validator script, and wp-integration (lines 181-195) allows only mirror paths and the openspec change directory.

Nit: wp-producers may update canonical bug-scrub and improve-harness skill documentation, but its write scope omits the corresponding skills/tests/bug-scrub and skills/tests/improve-harness documentation-contract suites.

Nit: Mapping the candidate's `priority` straight onto the roadmap item's `priority` produces duplicate priorities when the target is an existing roadmap. skills/refine-roadmap/scripts/refiner.py:165 defaults a new item's priority to max+1 precisely to avoid collisions, and only applies that default when the caller omits the field; supplying an explicit priority bypasses it. openspec/schemas/roadmap.schema.json:145 imposes no uniqueness constraint, so validation will not catch it, and only the reorder operation renumbers (refiner.py:340). A bug-scrub critical finding mapped to priority 1 and added to roadmap-supervisor-orchestration would tie with the existing ri-01, leaving execution order ambiguous for autopilot-roadmap.

Nit: D6 asserts that ri-13 must call this change's intake helper rather than build a second mapping, but nothing sequences ri-13 after ri-12, so ri-13 can execute first and the reuse contract silently fails. openspec/roadmaps/roadmap-supervisor-orchestration/roadmap.yaml:307-311 lists ri-13's depends_on as ri-02, ri-05, ri-11, ri-16 with no ri-12 edge, and both items are status approved. The plan cannot add the edge itself: proposal.md:104 puts direct roadmap writes out of scope, and openspec/roadmaps/** is denied in the wp-roadmap-intake and wp-integration scopes (work-packages.yaml:151, 197). The design states an intent with no enforcing mechanism.

Nit: The wp-producers verification command does not execute two of the four test directories the package is allowed to write, so tests placed there per the repo convention never run at the package gate. write_allow at lines 78-79 adds skills/tests/bug-scrub/** and skills/tests/improve-harness/**, matching the AGENTS.md rule that tests live in skills/tests/<skill-name>/, but the verification command at line 95 runs skills/bug-scrub/tests, skills/improve-harness/tests, skills/explore-feature/tests, and skills/tests/explore-feature only. skills/tests/improve-harness does not exist yet, and skills/tests/bug-scrub/test_skill_md.py is the invariant guard for the SKILL.md that task 1.2 modifies, so a broken SKILL.md passes wp-producers and surfaces only in the wp-integration full-suite run.

Nit: The bug-scrub category-to-effort table is not executable. design.md buckets simple diagnostics, test/deferred, and architecture/security/spec, but Finding.category also includes lint, type-error, and code-marker, which are never named in the mapping.

Nit: The inert-rendering / opaque-provenance security rule exists only in design.md and is absent from the skill-workflow and roadmap-orchestration spec deltas, so it is not a testable requirement for implementers or validators.

Nit: tasks.md Phase 1 implementation tasks depend only on their RED tests and omit 0.2, even though producer adapters need the shared validator/atomic writer created in 0.2; work-packages.yaml currently carries that ordering instead.

Nit: wp-contracts verification command includes skills/tests/prioritize-proposals/test_validate_candidate_work.py and task 0.2 updates the ri-11 CLI wrapper, but wp-contracts.write_allow omits skills/tests/prioritize-proposals/test_validate_candidate_work.py.
Nit: wp-producers includes skills/tests/bug-scrub/** in write_allow, but its verification command omits skills/tests/bug-scrub from the pytest invocation.

Nit: The determinism non-functional requirement is stated over input bytes alone, which is not achievable for the explore-feature adapter and is contradicted by the spec scenario it is meant to verify. proposal.md:87 sets the metric to "Same input bytes" yielding a byte-identical batch, but design.md:88-90 makes explore-feature eligibility depend on whether a change ID is absent from active and archived changes, which is repository state rather than input. specs/skill-workflow/spec.md:37 states the correct condition, "the same input and repository state". A VALIDATE phase testing the proposal's weaker wording would either pass vacuously or fail on an unrelated archive.

Optional: Bug-scrub is specified to promote every finding that passes its severity filter, and that filter defaults to the lowest band, so a routine scrub emits an unbounded candidate batch into the discovery back-edge. skills/bug-scrub/scripts/main.py:138 sets --severity to "low" by default across eight collectors including code markers, deferred issues, ruff, and mypy. Each surviving finding becomes one proposed OpenSpec change ID that ri-13's digest will later present for approval. The plan sets no cap, no promotion threshold distinct from the report threshold, and no grouping rule, and the non-functional requirements table carries no volume bound.

FYI: The shared module cannot be referred to by its literal repo path in any shipped skill text, which constrains the "canonical skill documentation" work in tasks 1.2, 1.4, 1.6, 2.2, and 3.3. skills/shared/validate_install_manifest.py:24-28 flags any line in a scanned SKILL.md or script matching `skills/shared/<file>` unless prefixed by .claude/ or .agents/, and install.sh runs that validator before syncing. Documentation must use the `<skill-base-dir>/../shared/candidate_work.py` idiom, as skills/refine-roadmap/SKILL.md already does for checkout_policy.py. The plan's own design.md and contracts/README.md use the literal path safely because openspec/ is outside the scanned payload.

The roadmap mutation boundary is correctly drawn and matches the existing implementation. D5 routes every existing-roadmap change through a refine-roadmap add request under preview and apply rather than writing roadmap.yaml, which is exactly the transaction skills/refine-roadmap/scripts/refiner.py implements with base_sha256 and append-only refinement records (openspec/schemas/roadmap.schema.json:75-115). The design's requirement that acceptance outcomes come from the operator rather than being invented also aligns with refiner._normalize_new_item at skills/refine-roadmap/scripts/refiner.py:159, which already rejects a new item lacking acceptance_outcomes, so the plan reinforces an existing invariant instead of duplicating or weakening it. The fail-closed write ordering in D2, validating the full batch before atomic replacement, is likewise specified with concrete failure semantics at design.md:120-126.

Optional: Failure semantics define user-facing refusals, but the plan adds no structured logging, stable error codes, or metrics for sidecar validation failures, mixed-batch ranking refusals, or intake collision/dependency failures.

FYI: Ranking treats unresolved active dependencies as blocked queue entries, while intake fails closed on unresolved dependencies. That stage difference is coherent, but a one-line cross-reference in design.md would prevent implementers from unifying the two behaviors by mistake.

Fail-closed persistence and mutation safety are well specified: full-batch validation before atomic sidecar replacement, no partial files, ranking refusal before scoring, and existing-roadmap changes only through refine-roadmap preview/apply.

The additive-sidecar approach correctly preserves rich producer artifacts, keeps the improve-harness legacy proposal flag for one migration window, and leaves the ri-11 candidate-work schema unchanged while centralizing validation in skills/shared.

FYI: The plan correctly establishes clear contracts for candidate-work generation, validation, ranking, and roadmap integration. The additive sidecar approach maintains backward compatibility while enabling deterministic processing.
FYI: The plan includes comprehensive test scenarios covering success cases, error conditions, and edge cases for all components. This demonstrates thorough thinking about validation requirements.
